items.title: Localization of a continuous function by axis-parallel cube integrals
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the ambient
convention under which the Lebesgue measure and integration interface used
below is stated ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, let
$U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $g:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuous.

For a closed axis-parallel cube $Q=\prod_{i<n}[a_i,a_i+\ell]\subseteq U$ with
$\ell>0$, the restriction $g|_Q$ is continuous on the compact nondegenerate
rectangle $Q$, hence bounded and Borel and Riemann integrable; denote by
$\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n$ the Lebesgue integral of $g$ over $Q$ with respect to
the restriction of Lebesgue measure, which by the comparison of the Riemann
and Lebesgue integrals equals the Riemann integral of $g$ over $Q$. Suppose
that

$$\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$$

for every closed axis-parallel cube $Q\subseteq U$ with side $\ell>0$. Then
$g=0$ on $U$.

In particular, for $n=2$, a continuous function on an open subset of the
plane whose integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in its
domain vanishes is identically zero.

The hypothesis requires every closed axis-parallel cube, with every centre and
every positive side length. A single cube does not suffice, and neither do the
cubes centred at one fixed point: on $U=\mathbb R^n$ the nonzero continuous
function $g(x)=x_0-p_0$ has $\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$ for every closed cube $Q$
centred at $p$, by cancellation in its first coordinate. This family also
differs from the family of closed cubes that merely contain $p$.
items.strategy: The Countable Choice convention is the Lebesgue interface of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. Suppose $g(p)\ne0$ for some $p\in U$; replacing $g$ by $-g$ if necessary, assume $g(p)>0$. By continuity at $p$ ([[def-metric-continuity]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) choose $\delta>0$ with $B(p,\delta)\subseteq U$ and $g(x)>g(p)/2$ whenever $d(x,p)<\delta$. The closed cube $Q:=p+[-\delta/(2\sqrt n),\delta/(2\sqrt n)]^n$ satisfies $Q\subseteq B(p,\delta)$, has side length $\ell=\delta/\sqrt n>0$ and satisfies $g\ge g(p)/2$ on $Q$. By [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], $\lambda_n(Q)=(2\delta/(2\sqrt n))^n=\ell^n>0$; the continuous $g$ is Borel measurable ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]) and bounded on the compact cube $Q$ ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]), so the signed integral over $Q$ is defined ([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Monotonicity and the scalar rules ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) give $\int_Qg\ge\int_Q(g(p)/2)\,d\lambda_n=(g(p)/2)\lambda_n(Q)>0$, contradicting the hypothesis $\int_Qg=0$. Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in U$. The planar clause is the case $n=2$. No regularity beyond continuity, and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is used.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Measure Theory (UC Davis lecture notes)
references.locator: Sets of finite measure and the measure of boxes; the localization argument uses only continuity, the positive measure of a nondegenerate cube and the monotonicity of the integral restricted to the cube, as in the notes' treatment of continuity against measure.

references.title: T. Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory (GSM 126), section 1.2
references.locator: Section 1.2, measure of boxes and the elementary properties of Lebesgue measure used in the localization argument.

items.title: Surface densities with vanishing test pairings vanish
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the surface-measure interface cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact
embedded $C^2$ hypersurface whose surface measure is that of the compact
embedded $C^1$ class of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] (the $C^2$ data are
special cases of the $C^1$ data), and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous.
Suppose that

$$\int_Sa\psi\,dS=0$$

for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]),
the pairing being the signed surface integral of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] of the continuous
function $a\,(\psi|_S)$. For complex tests the integral is defined componentwise in real and imaginary parts; the proof below uses real tests. Then $a=0$ on $S$. Equivalently, if two continuous
densities on $S$ pair equally against every test function, then they are equal
pointwise on $S$. The conclusion is pointwise and uses the continuity of $a$;
a merely locally integrable density would satisfy only an almost-everywhere
conclusion, which this statement does not claim.
items.strategy: Assume the stated Countable Choice convention. If $a(x_0)\ne0$, replace $a$ by $-a$ if needed and put $m=a(x_0)/2>0$. Continuity of $a$ on $S$ gives an ambient neighbourhood $N$ of $x_0$ on which $a\ge m$ on $S\cap N$. By the embedded $C^2$ hypothesis, the inverse/implicit-function suppliers give, after permuting coordinates, a graph chart $X(u)=(u,g(u))$ on an open $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $X(u_0)=x_0$ and $g\in C^2(D)$. Choose an open ambient chart neighbourhood $O\subset\Omega\cap N$ containing $x_0$, meeting $S$ only in this graph chart. Choose $0<r<R$ with $\overline B_R(x_0)\subset O$. The actual ambient bump supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] is a function $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(x_0)$; extended by zero it is in $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ by [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]. There is no product-extension assertion for arbitrary planar tests. By continuity of $X$, choose a closed nondegenerate parameter square $C\subset D$ around $u_0$ with $X(C)\subset B_r(x_0)$. The graph density is $J_X=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\ge1$ by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The surface measure and restriction to Borel chart subsets are exactly those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; chart independence lets the integral of a function supported in $S\cap O$ be computed in this chart. Equivalently one may choose a compact Jordan region $C'\Subset D$, obtained as a finite union of closed parameter squares lying in $D$ and covering the compact parameter preimage of its support and use [[thm-surface-integrals-over-c-one-graphs]] followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] for the continuous graph integrand on $C'$. On the support of $\psi|_S$ we have $a\ge m$, and $\psi=1$ on $X(C)$. Consequently monotonicity gives $\int_S a\psi\,dS\ge m\int_{X(C)}1\,dS=m\int_C J_X\,d\lambda_2\ge m\lambda_2(C)>0$; [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] gives $\lambda_2(C)=\ell^2>0$. This contradicts the given zero pairing. Every $x_0\in S$ therefore has $a(x_0)=0$, and applying this to the difference proves the equal-density clause. The compact embedded $C^2$ interface here is within the published compact embedded $C^1$ surface-measure class, with no change to its measure convention; in particular the closed stationary interfaces used by the jump theorem are covered. No new Choice principle is used. The empty-surface case is immediate.

items.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. For every closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$, its open interior $V=\prod_{i<3}(a_i,b_i)$ is a volume test geometry and $\overline V=K$. Its natural six-face presentation is the boundary of $K$, with outward normals $\pm e_i$. The volume variable is $V$, while $K$ denotes its compact closure. Each face is a degenerate three-dimensional box and hence has $\lambda_3$-measure zero by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]; their finite union $K\setminus V$ is null. Thus for continuous $h$ on a neighbourhood of $K$, $\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3=\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$: the positive and negative integrals over the null difference vanish by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]].

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
items.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the open box interior, with compact closure $K$, is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus. The requirement $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ makes clause (c)'s existing neighbourhood requirement explicit and restores the canonical definition contract. The closed-box integral bridge follows from the six degenerate faces being volume-null and the signed-integral definition, independently of their nonzero surface areas.

The definition is a convention for the integral form of the Maxwell equations; it asserts no field equation, no measurement and no apparatus realisation, and the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is inherited from the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions.

items.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]]
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of
distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]],
[[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing
$\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the
distributional partial derivatives are
$\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$
([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on
$U$ are identified with their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval,
let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map
$\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$
(coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],

$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$

define distributions on $U$ with
$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead
$I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the
absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint
events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with

$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$

([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source
therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included
explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or
endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded
$C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side
$\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]],
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let
$\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous
with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$; $\sigma$ carries C m$^{-2}$ and $K$ carries A m$^{-1}$ (a tangential surface current
density; the sheet is stationary). Then

$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$

define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner
integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the
functionals are bounded by
$(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection
of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one
with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of
this definition.

(d) [Unrestricted weak fields and optional interface branches] The general
field class for the solution predicate (e) consists of all locally integrable
pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, also when the source has a stationary-sheet part. No
classical one-sided trace or off-sheet $C^1$ regularity is required to define
those four distributional pairings. Additional trace hypotheses are optional
hypotheses of interface and jump results, not admission requirements of the
general weak model.

For a pointwise classical jump branch, one may additionally assume that $E,B$
are $C^1$ off $S\times I$ and, around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side
is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of
the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. These
joint one-sided extensions make the field traces and first spatial and
temporal derivatives continuous up to that side, locally uniformly on compact
cylinders.

For the broader weak-trace branch, retain spacetime $C^1$ regularity on
$(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and assume the original one-sided spatial
$C^1$ extensions at each time, with the explicit additional
conditions that the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the field traces are measurable and locally
integrable on $S\times I$ for $dS\,dt$. This branch supports sheet-distribution
and almost-everywhere jump identities; spatial continuity at each time gives
pointwise spatial identities for almost every time, and joint continuity of
the jump densities gives the further all-time upgrade. Separate spatial $C^1$
traces at each time alone do not imply that joint regularity or upgrade.
Whenever such traces exist, $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes their jump in the chosen
normal convention.

(e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a
field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source
distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable
volume densities with the charge and current quantity types of
[[def-em-sources]] (the weak predicate requires this stated
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity, not the classical continuous-source
regularity) and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b)
or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations
with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings

$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$

all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular
distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c).
This clause defines a solution predicate. When the singular parts vanish, its
four identities are the same as the locally integrable weak branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. That earlier postulate explicitly excludes point
and sheet distributions and does not imply their physical adoption here;
adoption for the declared singular-source models is made separately, after
this definition. No physical field equation is deduced merely from defining
this predicate.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields
occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test
function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary
surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or
$J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence
theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for
these sources is proved separately where used) and no regularisation. Sources
that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources,
moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are
outside the definition.
items.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) retains the unrestricted locally integrable field pair for the weak predicate, including sheet sources. It records optional interface hypotheses separately: joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions support the pointwise branch; the weaker per-time spatial C1 trace branch needs the explicit piecewise-derivative and sheet-trace L1 hypotheses for its distribution/a.e. conclusions. Neither branch is a general weak-field admission condition, and separate spatial C1 traces alone are not claimed to give joint continuity or temporal bounds. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition. The vanishing-pairing clause is a precise mathematical solution predicate. It agrees with the old postulate on its original locally integrable source class, but does not extend that physical postulate deductively to singular sources; physical adoption is a separate postulate. It remains possible for a declared source pair to be incompatible with those equations, and no existence is asserted.

items.physical_scope: The distributional source model and the weak solution predicate of the vacuum Maxwell equations in one named inertial frame: point sources along a C1 trajectory (with the finite-endpoint variant), stationary surface-charge and tangential surface-current sheets, locally integrable volume sources, locally integrable field pairs as the general weak class, and the optional one-sided trace branches used by interface results. The definition states what it means for a field-source tuple to satisfy the four distributional identities; it asserts no existence of solutions, no conservation law and no adoption of any field equation for singular sources.

items.design_state: necessary-physical-adoption-interface; proposal with source-backed nonproof formulation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared
distributional and surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the
flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive
constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following
additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or
stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the
volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy
its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$

are required in $\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning that all four residual pairings
defined there vanish for every compact smooth test. This is a physical adoption
of the classical vacuum idealisation in that source class, not a theorem about
sources and not a consequence of the original locally integrable source branch
of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. When the singular part vanishes, the adopted
identities coincide with that earlier weak branch.

Only source and field tuples satisfying these identities are models of this
postulate; the postulate does not assert existence for every prescribed source
pair, and compatibility conditions remain consequences to be checked. Sources
are the exact point and stationary-sheet types defined earlier, including their
properness or endpoint and tangential-current qualifications. No moving sheet,
line current, magnetic source, product of distributions, self-force,
regularisation, matter dynamics or material constitutive law is introduced.
This postulate reports no experiment or measurement and does not infer
empirical certainty from its mathematical formulation.
items.strategy: Nonproof formulation and scope review: adopt the already-defined four residual identities for the specified classical point/sheet source idealizations. Textbook point-delta and sheet-delta Maxwell treatments support this model choice; the exact compact-test formulation is supplied by the preceding definition. This is an explicit further physical premise, not an application of the old L1-only postulate outside its domain and not a fabricated deductive proof. The consistency/continuity and jump consequences belong to consuming conditional theorems.

items.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and
$\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and
$\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$

holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the
divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and
$\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on
$\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in
particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with
their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four
equations

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$

hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This
includes the original locally integrable weak branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source
models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source and
field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication
applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities
hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every
source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves
no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is
choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the
Countable Choice assumption of its defining source and surface-measure
formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
items.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

items.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of the
imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let
$E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the
volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the
fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional
derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$
jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every
volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$

and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions
$t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and
$t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for
every $t\in I$,

$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume
identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and
that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable
on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the
four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on
$\Omega\times I$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed
axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square
patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch,
and the divergence and curl of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.
items.strategy:
(a) Differential implies integral. Fix $t\in I$ and a volume test geometry $V$; $E(\cdot,t)$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$, so [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies (the theorem assumes the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) and gives $\oint_{\partial V}E\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\int_V\operatorname{div}E\,d\lambda_3=(1/\varepsilon_0)\int_V\rho\,d\lambda_3$ by the Gauss law of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the same computation with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ gives the second identity. For a patch test geometry, [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]] applied to the $C^1$ fields gives $\oint_{\partial S}E\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS$ with the induced orientation of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and $\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS=-\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$ by Faraday's law. The flux function is $t\mapsto\int_D\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv$, a Riemann integral over the compact Jordan parameter region of a function whose time derivative $\langle\partial_tB(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ is continuous on a neighbourhood of $D$ times a compact interval around $t$; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this Riemann integral with the Lebesgue integral to which [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] applies, giving differentiability on $I$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB\cdot n_S\,dS=\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$. Combining gives the Faraday identity; the Amp\`ere identity is the same with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

(b) Integral implies differential. Fix a point $p\in\Omega$, an index $i$, and the cyclic pair $(j,k)$ with $e_j\times e_k=e_i$. For every closed box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subset\Omega$ with positive sides take its admitted open interior $V$. The volume identities and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] give $\int_V(\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0)\,d\lambda_3=0$. The integrand $h=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and bounded on $K$. The six faces of $K\setminus V$ are volume-null by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] applied to the positive and negative parts gives $\int_Kh=\int_Vh=0$. In particular this holds for every closed cube $K\subset\Omega$; [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] gives $h=0$ on $\Omega$. The same argument applied to $h=\operatorname{div}B$ gives $\operatorname{div}B=0$. For the curl components, take the affine patch $r(u,v):=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over the square $D_\ell=[-\ell/2,\ell/2]^2$ (a patch test geometry whose parameter region is a rectangle and whose normal is $r_u\times r_v=e_i$); the Faraday identity of (b), Stokes' theorem and the differentiability of the flux function give $\int_{D_\ell}\bigl(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB\bigr)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i\,dudv=0$ for every sufficiently small $\ell>0$. Because the identities hold for every affine square patch contained in $\Omega$, for each fixed coordinate plane every closed square in its open slice is covered (translate its centre to $p$); this is the hypothesis of the planar clause of [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] for the continuous function $u\mapsto(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i$ on the corresponding coordinate plane; hence $(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)\cdot e_i=0$ at every point of $\Omega$, for each coordinate $e_i$. The same argument with the Amp\`ere identity gives $(\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE)\cdot e_i=0$. Therefore the four equations hold pointwise. The argument shows why a single selected test geometry is insufficient: the recovery uses the full families of boxes and affine square patches of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the convention of the divergence theorem and the surface-measure interface.

items.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source
fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a
chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side
$\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let
$\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous
with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current
density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on
$(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided
regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction
of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding
closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their
first space and time derivatives extend continuously to that side of
$S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be
continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on
$\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of
such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption
[[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak
Maxwell equations with the source pair

$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$

where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of
[[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in
the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts
$\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise
on $S\times I$,

$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$

with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is
$K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is
$\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its
normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make
$\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally
integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or
magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the
last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving
interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time
is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak-trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the
full locally integrable field and source class, without asserting undefined
classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields
have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in
addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are
measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$.
The one-sided traces are then locally integrable densities on the sheet, so
the four pairings
$$\int_I\int_S\bigl(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0\bigr)\psi\,dS\,dt,\quad\int_I\int_S(n\cdot[B])\psi\,dS\,dt,\quad\int_I\int_S(n\times[E])\psi\,dS\,dt,\quad\int_I\int_S\bigl(n\times[B]-\mu_0K\bigr)\psi\,dS\,dt$$
against every scalar $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$ (the vector integrals being componentwise) are well defined by the ordinary
surface-and-time integrals, with no product of distributions formed; these
vanishing pairings are the precise weak form of the four jump identities, and
they do vanish. The identities then hold for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$;
since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for
every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever
the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having
one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this
last upgrade.
items.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used.

items.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$
([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the **Gauss defects**

$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$

(a) [Smooth evolution branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$
$C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only
the two evolution equations

$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$

and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No
Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise.
For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints
at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists
with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero
initial Gauss defect.

(b) [Distributional evolution branch] The same derivative conclusion holds for
arbitrary scalar and vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the
two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in
$\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
This includes the original locally integrable field and source branch
identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class
when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$
distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$,
assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral and localization
interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In
this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time
persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is
assumed.

(c) [Full-Maxwell corollaries] Solutions with the regularity of (a) of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity
hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are
identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally integrable
weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point and
stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four
identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both
defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero
Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise
in (a) and distributionally in (b).

This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves
no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative
algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the
continuous-representative localization and the inherited declared
singular-source formulation.
items.strategy:
(a) Smooth algebra. For $C^2$ fields, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] give
$$\partial_tD_B=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tB)=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0,$$
and, with the positive commutation sign,
$$\partial_tD_E=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=c^2\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0.$$
Here $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the final equality is the separately assumed continuity, not a consequence of the evolution equations alone. The coordinate operators and product/linear rules are [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For fixed $x$, [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on compact subintervals of $I$ proves constancy, propagation and nonzero persistence.
(b) The identical componentwise cancellation holds for distributions by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], whose derivative-commutation clause is choice-free: in $\sum_{i,j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ the exchanged $i,j$ terms cancel. The two evolution identities and the independent continuity identity therefore give $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ without multiplying distributions.
For the continuous-representative conclusion, assume the stated Countable Choice and let $\partial_th=0$. Fix a spatial test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and put $F(t)=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)d\lambda_3(x)$. On any compact time subinterval the integrands have fixed compact spatial support and a uniform bound, by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]] and [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. Hence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] makes $F$ continuous. All products with compact temporal tests are absolutely integrable; [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify their multiple integrals with $\int_I F\eta$.
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ has zero integral, extend it by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)dv$. Equivalently start at a point strictly left of its support. The compact-test integral agrees with its Riemann integral by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] gives $H\prime=\eta$. Since the total integral is zero, $H$ vanishes both left and right of the support interval; it is smooth and compactly supported inside $I$. Therefore $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a legitimate compact test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$. Apply the derivative equation to THIS primitive test:
$$0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_I F(t)\eta(t)dt.$$
Choose a real nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ in $I$ with integral one, using [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] and the positive finite measure of an inner interval ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Decompose an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta_0=\eta-(\int_I\eta)\beta$. The preceding equality gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for every $\eta$, where $C:=\int_IF\beta$. A continuous function with all such pairings zero vanishes pointwise: if a real or imaginary component is nonzero, continuity gives a subinterval where that component has one sign and is bounded away from zero; a nonnegative bump supported there, equal to one on a smaller interval, contradicts integral monotonicity ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Thus $F$ is constant. The same argument for the continuous spatial difference $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$, now using bumps in $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, shows it is identically zero, since its pairing with every $\varphi$ is zero. This establishes independence of time. Compact support of every test, the actual derivative-test slot, and the public Countable Choice cost are explicit; no arbitrary-basepoint primitive is used.
(c) In the smooth full-Maxwell branch, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] supplies continuity, while Gauss gives $D_B=D_E=0$ directly; the original weak branch is the identical distributional argument. The separately adopted singular-source postulate uses the preceding solution predicate and the distributional continuity result. Conversely the propagated zero defects are exactly the missing two Gauss identities, so adding them to the evolution pair yields all four equations. No existence or empirical claim is inferred.

items.title: A suddenly appearing point charge with zero current is inadmissible
items.statement:
Let $q\ne0$ be a real charge parameter (coulombs) and let
$U:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the laboratory conventions of
[[def-em-weak-sources]]. Define a distribution $\rho$ on $U$ by

$$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_0^\infty\psi(0,t)\,dt,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$$

— an explicit switched-history distribution for $z(t)=0$ on $(0,\infty)$, with
no compensating current or source contribution at the appearance event; it does
not satisfy the proper-graph hypothesis of the zero-endpoint continuity branch
of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) — and let $J:=0$ be the zero distribution. Then:

(a) $\partial_t\rho=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}$ and $\operatorname{div}J=0$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), hence
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}\ne0$ in
$\mathcal D'(U)$: for every test function $\psi$,
$\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\,\psi(0,0)$,
because $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth with compact support. In particular the
continuity identity fails at the appearance event $(0,0)$.

(b) Consequently there are no locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $U$
satisfying the four weak residual identities of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e)
with the source pair $(\rho,0)$, the $\rho$-pairing being the explicit pairing
displayed above and $J=0$: such fields would satisfy the distributional
continuity identity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), which applies to
every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, and (a)
contradicts it. The source pair $(\rho,0)$ is therefore incompatible with the
formal four residual identities themselves; it is not one of the declared
point sources of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b), because the properness hypothesis
fails here as recorded, and no fields turn it into an admitted singular-source
model under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]].

(c) The failure is exactly the omitted endpoint term of the point-source
construction: by the endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
the same trajectory on a bounded interval $I_0=(a,b)$ has
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$
with $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$. A switched point charge with $J=0$ and no endpoint
or current term is thus inadmissible; a switched charge must be accompanied by
an explicit current or endpoint source term, which the weak equations of
[[def-em-weak-sources]] then require to satisfy continuity.

This is a mathematical incompatibility statement about a declared source
model, not a report of a measurement: no apparatus, sampling model,
uncertainty or empirical claim is involved.
items.strategy: Direct computation with the distributional definitions. (a) For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$ the pullback $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth and compactly supported, so $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-\langle\rho,\partial_t\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\psi(0,0)$ by the fundamental theorem of calculus on the support interval ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); the functional $\psi\mapsto q\psi(0,0)$ is $q\delta_{(0,0)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), which is nonzero because $q\ne0$ and some test function equals $1$ at $(0,0)$. Since $J$ is the zero distribution, $\operatorname{div}J=0$. (b) If locally integrable fields $E,B$ satisfied the four weak equations in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the distributional pair $(\rho,0)$, then [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) — stated for arbitrary distributional source pairs satisfying the four equations — would give $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$, contradicting (a). (c) The endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] computes the endpoint deltas of a finite-history point source; setting $J=0$ while retaining the charge history $(0,\infty)$ is precisely the omission of those endpoint terms. Nothing here is a physical claim about charge creation: it states that the declared source model fails its own continuity requirement, and it exhibits the general statement of the previous item on an explicit example. The item inherits the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-em-weak-sources]], on whose clause (b) it depends, and records it in its dependencies; the computation itself is choice-free and uses neither the surface-measure interface nor any selection. The adopted physical singular-source equations are now supplied by [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; the original weak postulate excludes singular densities. The nonexistence proof is stronger than any source-admission question, since the four formal residual identities themselves imply the continuity that the switched history violates.

items.title: Surface independence of the total current flux and the role of the displacement term
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of
[[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region
$D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches
span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open
region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation
whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with
outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal
induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches;
this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]

$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$

where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of
[[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of
the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the
displacement fluxes:

$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$

Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement
fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations
alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] In this clause all displayed variables and constants are numerical values in the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: spatial coordinates in metres, $t$ in seconds, $E$ in V m$^{-1}$, $B$ in T, $\rho$ in C m$^{-3}$ and $J$ in A m$^{-2}$. Thus the profile argument $z$ means physical height divided by $1\,\mathrm m$, the implicit current-density scale is $1\,\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and the geometric length scale is $1\,\mathrm m$. The following declared smooth data satisfies all
the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two
surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb
R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for
$z\ge0$, and set

$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$

Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$,
$\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because
$c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$.
Take $D=[-1,1]^2$ and its interior $D^\circ=(-1,1)^2$. Let $\sigma$ be the
standard smooth step of [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] and define
$h(s):=\sigma(2(1-s^2))$, $\eta(u,v):=h(u)h(v)$. Then
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a
neighbourhood of the origin, $\eta>0$ at every point of $D^\circ$, and $\eta=0$
on $\partial D$ and outside $D$. Take the graphs

$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$

Both induced boundary chains are the square
$\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region
$V=\{(u,v,w):(u,v)\in D^\circ,\ -2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the
patches, and

$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$

the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so
$\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive,
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop
integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard
charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction
current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement
term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a
self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source
type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not
an additional empirical claim.
items.strategy: (a) Put $G:=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$. By the smooth Gauss law and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], $\operatorname{div}G=\operatorname{div}J+\varepsilon_0\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho=0$ on that neighbourhood, the last equality being continuity, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applied to $G$ on the specified presentation of $V$ — outward normal $-n_1$ on the face $S_1$ and $+n_2$ on the face $S_2$ — gives $0=\int_V\operatorname{div}G=\int_{S_2}G\cdot n_2-\int_{S_1}G\cdot n_1$, which is the first asserted equality. The equality with $(1/\mu_0)\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r$ is Ampere's integral identity of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]](a) applied to either patch, whose induced boundary chain is $\gamma$; the two patches consequently give the same circulation. (b) Split $G$ in the equality of (a); this is algebra with the definitions of the fluxes ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) and no further analytic input. (c) Verify the smooth equations for the displayed data by direct substitution: $\operatorname{div}E=(t/\varepsilon_0)\chi'(z)$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$; $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}(E_z(z,t)e_z)=0$ because $E_z$ is independent of $x$ and $y$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB=0$; $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ and $\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE=-\mu_0\chi(z)e_z+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\chi(z)e_z=0$ since $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=\chi'(z)-\chi'(z)=0$. The standard step is smooth, is zero for arguments at most zero, is one for arguments at least one and is strictly positive on $(0,1)$ ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]]). Thus $h$ is smooth, positive for $|s|<1$, one for $|s|\le1/\sqrt2$ and zero for $|s|\ge1$; the product $\eta$ has exactly the declared properties. In particular the entire open square has positive graph separation, rather than merely a central subregion. Both graph maps are smooth and injective regular parametrizations on a neighbourhood of $D$, since their first two coordinates are $(u,v)$ and their area vectors are $(-\varphi_u,-\varphi_v,1)$. Their induced square boundary chains coincide at height zero. The explicitly restricted $V$ is nonempty, bounded and open, with compact closure contained in $[-1,1]^2\times[-2,0]$; its boundary is exactly $S_1\cup S_2$. Strict positivity of $\eta$ on $D^\circ$ gives $S_1\cap S_2=\partial D\times\{0\}$. This square seam is a compact union of four line segments, has surface measure zero on each regular graph face, and contains the relative face boundaries. At every point off the seam the boundary is locally the single smooth graph with $V$ above the lower graph and below the upper graph. The faces therefore give the actual finite presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]], with outward normals $-n_1,+n_2$, without overlapping positive-area face pieces. For $\varphi_1=-2\eta$, the induced upward unit normal is $n_1=(2\eta_u,2\eta_v,1)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$, so $(J\circ r_1)\cdot n_1=-\chi(-2\eta)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$; after multiplication by its area Jacobian the pullback density is $(J\circ r_1)\cdot(r_{1,u}\times r_{1,v})=-\chi(-2\eta)$. For the plane $n_2=e_z$ and the density is $-\chi(0)=0$. The graph flux formula thus gives exactly the two stated integrals, with the unit-normal scalar distinguished from the unnormalized area-vector density. On any ball $B(0,r)$ with $0<r<1/2$, $\eta=1$ and $\chi(-2\eta)=1$. The nonnegative continuous integrand has strictly positive integral on $D$, by the Riemann/Lebesgue comparison, monotonicity and positive ball area already declared; its negative is the strictly negative lower conduction flux, as stated. The total fluxes both vanish because $G=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE=-\chi(z)e_z+\chi(z)e_z=0$, consistent with the vanishing circulation of $B=0$. The explicit step-product supplies the required positivity on the entire square interior; the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the test-geometry, surface-measure and divergence-theorem items, and no further choice is used.
